notes: Evaluation focused on latency SLOs and measurement alignment. Customer requires clear separation of server-side inference timing vs end-to-end client timing. They want: p50/p95/p99 specified for both non-streaming (request -> full response) and streaming (time-to-first-token, per-token tail). Target thresholds discussed: non-streaming p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 550ms for single-turn chat with t2-medium models; streaming time-to-first-token <= 120ms and per-token p95 <= 60ms for 99th percentile of interactive sessions. Important: Auriga insists metrics be measured client-side (their app) and correlated with server-side traces; they require trace IDs, consistent clock sync (NTP), and a small sampling of full traces for p99 debugging. Agreed conventions: "server_infer_time_ms" = runtime from model runtime entry to last token emitted; "e2e_time_ms" = client request send timestamp -> final token received; "ttft_ms" = first byte/token. Measurement notes: use histogram buckets for tail percentiles, export p50/p95/p99 and stable rate (tokens/sec) daily; retain raw spans for 30 days for audit. For reserved GPU planning we proposed: guaranteed pool of 8 A100-like GPUs, baseline throughput guarantee 12k tokens/s sustained, burst headroom to 18k tokens/s with warm KV cache. Batching guidance: prefer small dynamic batching (max batch 8) to maintain latency SLOs; pre-warm KV cache during soak. Fallbacks: automatic routing to 8-bit quantized model variant with slightly higher p95 but lower cost under heavy load. SLA negotiation points: uptime 99.95%, latency SLO credit policy (credit if >1% of minutes in a month have p99 misses), error budget of 0.5% p99 misses monthly. Support: 2h P1 response, dedicated escalation channel. CTO quote: "We can't accept unpredictable tails — p99 is a hard requirement for front-line pricing decisions." Next deliverables: formal SLO doc with measurement recipes, soak test plan, reserved-pool contract draft.
requirements_summary: Workload: interactive pricing chat + document reranking. Latency targets: p50/p95/p99 both server and end-to-end; explicit streaming metrics (ttft, per-token). Throughput: baseline 12k tokens/s reserved, burst to 18k tokens/s. Model preferences: MPT-style open model variants + locked quantized fallback. Routing: region-first, VPC-only, automatic fallback to quantized variant. Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS integration, data residency in us-east-1. Measurement alignment: client instrumentation + correlated server spans, percentile histograms, 30d trace retention.
